 Coram: Justice V. Narasingh

Order
21.07.2023 Order No.
04. 1.
None appears for the informant when the matter is called.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

3. The petitioner is an accused in C.T. Case No.624 of 2023, pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Chandikhole, arising out of Jenapur P.S. Case No.90 of 2023, for commission of alleged offences under Sections 419/420 of IPC.

4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chandikhole, by order dated 06.05.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
5. It is stated by the learned counsel that the petitioner is in custody since 23.04.2023 on the allegation that he duped the informant-lady a sum of Rs.2,30,000/-.
6. It is submitted by the learned counsel that since charge sheet has been filed in the meanwhile,
further continuance of the petitioner in custody is unwarranted.
7. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.
8. Taking into account the nature of allegation, this Court directs the petitioner to be released on Binod Chandra Behera vs State Of Odisha ....

1 bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.
9. While releasing the petitioner on bail, learned Court in seisin is called upon to verify the criminal antecedent of similar nature.
If it comes to the fore that the petitioner has any such criminal antecedent, this order shall stand recalled.

10. Learned counsel for the petitioner on instruction undertakes to deposit upfront a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees fifty thousand) and rest of Rs.1,80,000/-/-(Rupees one lakh eighty thousand)
within a period of six months in six equal installments.

11. In view of such undertaking, it is directed that the petitioner shall upfront pay a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees fifty thousand) and the balance amount of Rs.1,80,000/-(Rupees one lakh eighty thousand) shall be paid in six monthly installments.
The first of such monthly installments shall fall due after four months of the release of the petitioner.
12. Learned Court in seisin to fix the quantum of each of the installments.
13. The amount so deposited shall be kept in an interest bearing account which shall be subject to the outcome of the lis.
14. It shall be open to the informant to seek release of the said amount in accordance with law.

15. It is made clear that the amount deposited as aforesaid is without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the petitioner and this Court has not expressed any opinion regarding his complicity of the petitioner which has to be adjudicated in an independent manner in the impending trial.
16.
The amount for deposit is being directed as a deterrent and in view of the undertaking.
17. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
18. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
(V  Ayesha
